paper: KODA: Kinematics–Observation Data Alignment for Humanoid Learning from Human Egocentric Demonstration

figures.caption: Overview of KODA. Whole-Body Motion Generation produces simulation-feasible whole-body motion from human egocentric demonstrations, and Robot Onboard View Generation synthesizes motion-aligned onboard views. The motion, views, and task instruction form a reusable canonical record. Control Command Generation uses this record to generate controller-specific states and actions. The resulting data are combined with matching real-robot demonstrations to co-train a controller-specific vision-language-action (VLA) policy for language-guided humanoid loco-manipulation.

figures.caption: KODA pipeline. Middle: Human demonstrations become aligned whole-body motion and onboard observations, then controller-specific state-action data for VLA training (Control Command Generation). Top: Whole-Body Motion Generation combines hand estimation and contact-aware retargeting, sampling-based command optimization (SCO), and arm refinement. Bottom: Robot Onboard View Generation combines arm removal, scene reprojection, robot rendering, depth compositing, and inpainting. Input depth is observed or estimated from RGB.

figures.caption: Sampling-based command optimization (SCO) uses CEM to optimize sparse pose residuals through sampling, rollout, evaluation, and proposal updates.
